introduction:
A Registered Will is a pivotal legal instrument that ensures your assets and properties are distributed precisely according to your final wishes. By formally registering the Will under the Indian Registration Act, 1908, you provide it with an undisputed legal backing, significantly minimizing the chances of future familial disputes or fraudulent claims in Madhya Pradesh.

Registration ensures the document is safely preserved in the official government custody (Book No. 3), providing an authentic reference that cannot be easily tampered with, destroyed, or forged.
quickFacts:
Quick Facts
  • Topic: How to initiate and register a Will (वसीयत) online using the Madhya Pradesh SAMPADA 2.0 portal.
  • Platform: SAMPADA 2.0 web portal (sampada.mpigr.gov.in).
  • Parties Involved: A minimum of 3 individuals are required (1 Testator/Executor who makes the Will, and 2 Witnesses).
  • Stamp Duty: ₹0 (Will registration is exempt from stamp duty in MP).
  • Registration Fee: ₹1,000.
  • Mandatory Action: Even after completing the online application and e-signing, an offline physical visit to the Sub-Registrar Office (SRO) by all parties is required to finalize the registration.
documentsRequired:
Documents Required for Will Registration

Note: Ensure all details match your Aadhaar database before beginning the online registration process.
Mandatory Identifications & Details
  • Valid Mobile Number (must be active for receiving OTPs).
  • Valid Email ID.
  • Aadhaar Card: Mandatory for the Executor and both Witnesses for e-KYC and e-Signing.
  • PAN Card (Optional but recommended if applicable).
Will Draft & Verification Credentials
  • Digital copy of the drafted Will: Can be typed directly into the portal or pasted in Word format; supports Hindi and English.
  • Biometric Device (Optional: only needed if you prefer to authenticate Aadhaar via fingerprint/iris instead of mobile OTP).
  • Digital Signature Certificate / DSC (Optional: if signing via DSC instead of Aadhaar-based e-Sign).
  • Original physical ID proofs and passport-sized photographs (Required later for the physical SRO visit).
onlineApplication:
Method 1: Online Process via SAMPADA 2.0

  1. Step 1: Login & Initiate: Log in to the SAMPADA 2.0 portal. Navigate to the e-Registry tab and click on Initiate e-Registry. Read the instructions and declarations carefully.
  2. Step 2: Select Document Type: Under 'Select Document Type', choose Miscellaneous from the dropdown, and then select Will Deed. Click Save and Next.
  3. Step 3: Add Party Details (Executor & Witnesses):
    • First, add the Executor's details. Select the applicant type (Individual/Organization).
    • Perform Aadhaar e-KYC using an OTP (sent to the Aadhaar-linked mobile), Fingerprint, or Iris scan.
    • Fill in the demographic details (Name, Father/Husband's Name, DOB, Category, Religion, and Address). Click Save.
    • Repeat this exact e-KYC and detail-filling process to add Witness 1 and Witness 2.
  4. Step 4: Duty Details: Go to the 'Other Details' section, review the transaction, and verify the fee breakdown (Stamp Duty: ₹0, Registration Fee: ₹1000). Click Save and Next.
  5. Step 5: Deed Drafting: Select the document language (Hindi or English). Type or paste your written Will into the text box provided. Click Save as Draft, then click View Deed and Final Submit, and confirm the submission.
  6. Step 6: Payment: Proceed to the payment section. Pay the ₹1,000 registration fee using the portal wallet or the online payment gateway.
  7. Step 7: Accept and e-Sign: Go to the Sign off All Party(s) tab. An SMS link will be sent to the parties. Click Take Electronic Sign next to each party's name and digitally sign the document using Aadhaar-based e-Sign (C-DAC / eMudhra) or a DSC.
  8. Step 8: Slot Booking: Once all signatures are electronically captured, move to the Slot Booking section. Select your preferred Sub-Registrar Office (SRO) and book a time slot for your physical visit.
  9. Step 9: Offline Visit (Mandatory): On the booked date and time, the Executor and both Witnesses must physically visit the selected Sub-Registrar Office. The Sub-Registrar will verify your original identities, capture physical signatures/biometrics if required, and finalize the legal registration of the Will.
offlineApplication:
Method 2: Traditional Offline Registration

Note: The standard legal offline process for registering a Will in India is detailed below.
  1. Step 1: Draft the Will: Write or type your Will clearly on a plain piece of paper (Stamp paper is not legally mandatory for a Will). Clearly mention your assets, bank details, and the respective beneficiaries.
  2. Step 2: Witness Attestation: The testator (maker of the Will) must sign the document in the presence of at least two reliable witnesses. The witnesses must also sign the Will.
  3. Step 3: Visit the Sub-Registrar Office: The testator and the two witnesses must physically visit the Sub-Registrar Office that has jurisdiction over the testator's residence.
  4. Step 4: Document Submission: Submit the original drafted Will, passport-sized photographs of all three parties, and valid ID/Address proofs (Aadhaar, PAN, etc.).
  5. Step 5: Pay Fees: Pay the nominal government Will registration fee at the counter.
  6. Step 6: Final Registration: The Sub-Registrar will verify the identities of the testator and witnesses, record their statements, and officially register the Will, providing it with a government seal and registration number.
afterApplying:
After Registration & Storage Guidelines

  • Following the successful physical verification at the Sub-Registrar Office, the Will becomes a legally registered document stored securely in government records.
  • You can track the status on the SAMPADA portal. Once processed, you will be able to download a certified digital copy (E-Registered Document) directly from your dashboard using your Registration ID.
  • It is highly recommended to store the original physical copy of the registered Will in a safe place (like a bank locker) and inform your trusted family members or the appointed executor of its location.
